output.brief: The cancellation rise is mainly a Quillbook accounting-sync problem, not a price problem. Since 30 March, the Quillbook connector has lost or doubled about 58,300 invoices across 1,212 accounts. By 31 July, 34% of those accounts had cancelled, against 8% of unaffected ones. Repriced accounts with no connector barely moved (1.8% to 1.9%), and Founders accounts on Quillbook rose sharply even though their price did not change. The price rise did contribute at the start, but the April data alone could not separate it from the sync failures. Tallymarsh changes are within normal noise, and seasonality and the mobile release do not fit the pattern. I am fairly confident in this, but the Tallymarsh log has never been reviewed. Next: make the Quillbook fix (move to v3) a top priority, now rated Sev-3 and unscheduled, and contact affected accounts to correct invoices. Keep the duplicate-invoice hold on, since it blocks 3,870 duplicates. Hold off on the price reversal and the Tallymarsh rebuild until the Tallymarsh log is reviewed.
